$comment: Canonical, NON-SECRET deployment-target registry for scripts/ci/production-target-guard.mjs.
A Supabase project ref is a public routing identifier, not an authentication secret: it appears
in every URL the browser sends. It is recorded here so a target can be COMPARED, and nowhere
else, so there is exactly one place to change when the owner rotates or moves a project.
canonicalProductionRef is set from the REPOSITORY OWNER'S DECLARATION. The owner knows their
own deployment; that is authority. It is NOT a reading of the deployed Railway runtime, which
no verifying environment has been able to reach, and it is deliberately not recorded as one.
See identityBasis below and deploymentIdentity in CURRENT_STATE.attestation.json.
Setting it does NOT make deployment unconditional. This guard still resolves the target from
the environment it is actually run in and rejects anything that is not this ref. A declaration
fixes the expected answer; the guard checks the environment in front of you against it.
OWNER UPDATE PROCEDURE is documented in docs/runbooks/deployment-target-guard.md.
identityBasisNote: Declared by the repository owner in the 'Production Identity and Supabase Preview Integrity' follow-up work order, 2026-08-26. Corroborated by read-only catalog evidence (see the entry below). NOT independently read from the deployed Railway service: the egress policy answered 403 to CONNECT for the live app host, so that evidence class was unobtainable in this environment.

knownRefs.note: Canonical production, established by REPOSITORY OWNER DECLARATION and corroborated by read-only catalog evidence: governed ledger 79 with this repository's tail, 119 public tables whose sha256 over sorted names matches the local replay exactly, 54 enums, 17 views, all four governed marker tables, 8 receiving RPCs, migration 80 not applied. The corroboration is what a database CONTAINS; the owner declaration is what makes it canonical. Its display name contains 'production'; that played no part in the classification, and never may.

Target of the repository's Supabase Preview GitHub check, whose preview branching is DISABLED, so the check is a permanent no-op. Structurally far behind this repository. Displayed under a name that reads like the product, which is exactly what makes it dangerous.
